elements.element: Customer owns deliverables and work product created for it
elements.evidence: "all customization work, client front ends, deliverables and work product created by Licensor specifically for Licensee ... shall be owned by Licensee" (narrowed by "and paid for by Licensee")

elements.element: Vendor assigns such deliverables/work product to Customer
elements.evidence: "Licensor hereby assigns all right, title and interest therein to Licensee"
"Licensor retains ownership of its pre-existing Intellectual Property Rights and the Platform Software"

elements.element: Perpetual, irrevocable, royalty-free licence to any Vendor IP embedded in deliverables
elements.evidence: "licence to use, modify and sublicense any Licensor Intellectual Property Rights embedded in such deliverables" — "Intellectual Property Rights" is a defined, enumerated category list of Licensor rights rather than any Vendor IP embedded in the deliverables

elements.element: Customer retains all rights in Customer Data
elements.evidence: "Licensee retains all right, title and interest in and to all data, information and content submitted, transmitted or generated by or on behalf of Licensee"
"no Licensee Data, deliverable or work product shall be jointly owned by the parties"

elements.element: Vendor owns generic tools and know-how
elements.evidence: "Licensor owns all right, title, and interest in and to the Licensed Technology" (Licensed Know-How and Licensed Software) and "retains ownership of its pre-existing Intellectual Property Rights and the Platform Software"

elements.element: Customer receives perpetual, irrevocable, worldwide, royalty-free licence to deliverables
elements.evidence: "perpetual, irrevocable, worldwide, royalty-free licence"; deliverables themselves are assigned outright to Licensee, exceeding a licence

elements.element: Licence rights to use, modify and sublicense for Customer's business
elements.evidence: "to use, modify and sublicense any Licensor Intellectual Property Rights embedded in such deliverables for Licensee's business purposes"

reasons: Preferred is incomplete on one element: the embedded-IP licence is tied to the defined term "Intellectual Property Rights" (an enumerated Licensor category list) instead of any Vendor IP embedded in the deliverables, so residual embedded Vendor material outside that definition is unlicensed.

Minimality fails because the insertion imports fallback-only rights ("worldwide", "modify", "sublicense") into a preferred-level proposal, duplicating protection alongside outright assignment of the deliverables.
The added condition "and paid for by Licensee" narrows preferred deliverable ownership beyond what the position requires and creates a payment-contingent ownership mechanic.

Intent is preserved: Article III's Licensor ownership of the Licensed Technology, the notice and anti-copying covenants, and the Article VII(b) further-work mechanic all remain effective, and "Licensee Data" is defined where introduced.
Assessed at fallback on material terms, so this would be noted in the rationale rather than escalated, but the drafter's locked preferred target is not fully achieved.
